analysis: The PR adds one allowlisted env key, SSDPrefixCachePolicy.incrementalCheckpointsFlag (DARKBLOOM_PREFIX_CACHE_SSD_INCREMENTAL_CHECKPOINTS), to LaunchAgent.inferencePassthroughEnvKeys (head line 375) and doc comments (head 332-334). A test was added in LaunchAgentRestartTests.swift (lines 336-360). The change only affects which operator-set env values are forwarded into the launchd plist EnvironmentVariables. passthroughEnvironment (head 418-439) still forwards only allowlisted, non-empty keys. The test checks that unrelated secrets are excluded and that the watchdog does not receive the key. The new key does not touch the plist structure, program arguments, binary path, Apple attestation, coordinator trust, or authorization flow. Related threat T-041 (SSD prefix cache): the flag controls delta vs. complete-file checkpoint writing. The supplied evidence does not include SSDPrefixCachePolicy or the SSDBlockStore delta format. So I cannot confirm whether delta checkpoints keep the T-041 invariants: HMAC-only names, GCM AAD with no prompt-derived metadata beyond lookupTag, salt scoping, TTL/LRU purge, and KEK-wipe purge. The default-on delta behaviour is an at-rest format change that the threat-model entry for T-041 may need to describe, and it should be reviewed in the files that implement it (the SSDPrefixCache* sources, not in this batch). From the files here, I found no concrete regression. A local operator who can set the plist env already controls the provider (ADV-001/TB-003), and the flag only toggles a cache format rollback. Remaining question: confirm in the SSD cache implementation that delta checkpoint files preserve the authentication, HMAC-naming and TTL guarantees, and that rollback-to-complete does not leave stale delta artifacts unpurged.
